module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 87

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/87](https://www.erdosproblems.com/87)
- [Er95] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and geometry.
  Resenhas (1995), 165-186.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos87

/--
Let $0 < \epsilon < 1$. Is it true that, if $k$ is sufficiently large, then
$$R(G) > (1-\epsilon)^k R(k)$$
for every graph $G$ with chromatic number $\chi(G)=k$?

The restriction $\epsilon < 1$ excludes negative bases in $(1-\epsilon)^k$.

This problem is #12 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_87.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ε < 1 → ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = (k : ℕ∞) →
        (SimpleGraph.diagonalGraphRamsey G : ℝ) >
          (1 - ε) ^ k * (SimpleGraph.diagonalRamsey k : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Even stronger, is there some $c > 0$ such that, for all large $k$,
$$R(G) > c R(k)$$
for every graph $G$ with chromatic number $\chi(G)=k$?

This problem is #13 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_87.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = (k : ℕ∞) →
        (SimpleGraph.diagonalGraphRamsey G : ℝ) > c * (SimpleGraph.diagonalRamsey k : ℝ) := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos87

reformulations.difference: The linked UCSD Ramsey problem #12 requires the number of vertices n to be sufficiently large. Lean instead requires the chromatic number k to be sufficiently large, agreeing with the current erdosproblems.com statement.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For finite G, χ(G) ≤ |V(G)| ≤ R(G). Thus a vertex-count threshold implies a chromatic-number threshold. Conversely, given a chromatic threshold K for a fixed ε, choose a vertex threshold greater than all the finitely many values (1−ε)^k R(k) with k<K. These remaining cases then follow from R(G) ≥ |V(G)|. The equivalence, including the universal ε quantifier, was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean using Review87.eventual_chromatic_iff_order.

reformulations.difference: The linked UCSD Ramsey problem #13 asks for an absolute positive lower bound on R(G)/R(k) for all graphs. Lean uses R(G)>c R(k) for sufficiently large k, agreeing with the current erdosproblems.com statement.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For positive k, R(k)>0, so the quotient and product inequalities are equivalent. If an eventual bound holds with c>0 above a threshold K, replace c by min(c, 1/(1+Σ_{j<K} R(j))). For 1≤k<K the new right-hand side is strictly less than 1≤R(G); above K the original bound applies. The converse is immediate. Both the removal of finitely many exceptional positive k and the quotient/product equivalence were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: Both declarations are faithful; the current Erdős page still records the problem as OPEN. The restriction ε<1 is explicitly present in linked UCSD problem #12 and matches its intended small-ε formulation. Inspected the ordinary, non-induced-copy Ramsey definitions and chromatic-number semantics. Lean checks established nonemptiness of the Ramsey defining sets for finite graphs, R(G)≥|V(G)|, χ(K_k)=k, and R(0)=0, R(1)=1, R(2)=2. The boundary and equivalence proofs use no sorry or target conjecture. The full text of [Er95] could not be retrieved; comparisons were completed using the cited Erdős page and its two linked UCSD restatements.
